claims.statement: Every nontrivial zero rho of zeta satisfies Re(rho)=1/2.
The existing c=2 trace/Frobenius/positive-index certificate is simultaneously extremal on online doubles and tight off-line pairs and cannot be improved using only those quantities.
For an absolutely summable spectral zero filter, any off-line zero with nonzero filter coefficient forces the corresponding filtered zero family to fail the subexponential bound.
For the frozen Weil-admissible R001 filter and exact arithmetic residual, existence of an off-line zero forces failure of the subexponential bound.
The same frozen Weil-admissible R001 residual family is subexponential from unconditional arithmetic/prime-side estimates.
A predeclared multi-probe family separates a tight off-line pair from an online double in a theorem-relevant way not reducible to TightMult-visible data.
A finite CCM object is connected to the Weil/aperture object by an exact identity, intertwiner, or controlled convergence theorem sufficient for route closure.
